BURSEVI:v4p173#2/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v4p173#2/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v4p173#2/r4.claim: Dāʾban is an adverbial verbal noun meaning they should farm continuously and diligently, following their usual practice.
BURSEVI:v4p173#2/r4.anchor: مصدر دأب في العمل إذا جد فيه وتعب وانتصابه على الحالية

BURSEVI:v4p173#2/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v4p173#2/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v4p173#2/r5.claim: Harth is sowing seed and preparing soil, while zarʿ is tending and growing the crop; zarʿ is broader because it can also mean sowing, while God causes growth.
BURSEVI:v4p173#2/r5.anchor: والفرق بين الحرث والزرع أن الحرث القاء البذر وتهيئة الأرض

BURSEVI:v4p173#2/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v4p173#2/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v4p173#2/r6.claim: Joseph forecast seven abundant years and recommended leaving grain in its ears to protect it from pests; green ears may have suggested this unusual storage method.
BURSEVI:v4p173#2/r6.anchor: اتركوه فيه ولا تذروه كيلا يأكله السوس كما هو شأن غلال مصر

BURSEVI:v4p174/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v4p174/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v4p174/r1.claim: They should eat only a little during the seven plentiful years and store the rest; Joseph’s instruction teaches restraint and economy.
BURSEVI:v4p174/r1.anchor: مما تأكلون في تلك السنين فأنتم تدرسون وقت حاجتكم إليه

FARISI-HUJJA:v4p424#2/r1.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v4p424#2/r1.speaker: ابن كثير ونافع وأبو عمرو وابن عامر وحمزة والكسائي
FARISI-HUJJA:v4p424#2/r1.claim: They read دأبًا with a quiescent hamza; Abu Amr drops the hamza when reciting in connected flow.
FARISI-HUJJA:v4p424#2/r1.anchor: فقرأ ابن كثير ونافع وأبو عمرو وابن عامر، وحمزة، والكسائي: دأبا ساكنة الهمزة

FARISI-HUJJA:v4p424#2/r2.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v4p424#2/r2.speaker: حفص عن عاصم
FARISI-HUJJA:v4p424#2/r2.claim: Hafs reports دأبًا with fatḥa on hamza, whereas Abu Bakr reports it quiescent; the source also records a fatḥa transmission from Asim.
FARISI-HUJJA:v4p424#2/r2.anchor: وروى حفص عن عاصم: دأبا بفتح الهمزة. وروى أبو بكر

FARISI-HUJJA:v4p424#2/r3.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v4p424#2/r3.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v4p424#2/r3.claim: Quiescence is the more common form; fatḥa may be a dialect variant like شمع/شمع, and دأبًا is accusative after تزرعون.
FARISI-HUJJA:v4p424#2/r3.anchor: الأكثر في دأب* الإسكان، ولعل الفتح لغة

IBNMUJAHID:v1p349/r1.author: Ibn Mujāhid
IBNMUJAHID:v1p349/r1.speaker: حفص عن عاصم
IBNMUJAHID:v1p349/r1.claim: Ḥafṣ reads دأبا with fatḥa on hamza; Abū Bakr transmits sukūn from ʿĀṣim, while Mūsā al-Zābī reports fatḥa like Ḥafṣ.
IBNMUJAHID:v1p349/r1.anchor: وروى حفص عن عاصم ﴿ دأبا ﴾ بفتح الهمزة وروى أبو بكر عنه ساكنة الهمزة

QIRAAT-ER:12:47:5#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:12:47:5#1/r1.speaker: author
QIRAAT-ER:12:47:5#1/r1.claim: The standard form fully vocalizes daʾab with hamza fatḥa and tanwīn.
QIRAAT-ER:12:47:5#1/r1.anchor: Standard canonical form — hamza with fatḥa + tanwīn; full voweling of daʾab

QIRAAT-ER:12:47:5#2/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:12:47:5#2/r1.speaker: author
QIRAAT-ER:12:47:5#2/r1.claim: Sukūn on hamza removes its following vowel without changing meaning.
QIRAAT-ER:12:47:5#2/r1.anchor: Variant with sukūn on hamza (daʾban) — elision of second vowel; same meaning

QIRAAT-ER:12:47:5#3/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:12:47:5#3/r1.speaker: author
QIRAAT-ER:12:47:5#3/r1.claim: Another variant drops hamza entirely as a phonological simplification.
QIRAAT-ER:12:47:5#3/r1.anchor: Variant dropping hamza entirely → dāban; phonological simplification

QIRAAT-ER:12:47:5#4/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:12:47:5#4/r1.speaker: author
QIRAAT-ER:12:47:5#4/r1.claim: The pausal form is dābā, followed by daʾban on resuming recitation.
QIRAAT-ER:12:47:5#4/r1.anchor: Pausal form dābā with subsequent recitation as daʾban — phonological pause variant

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p285/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p285/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p285/r1.claim: Joseph's reply combines three kinds of speech: interpretation by meaning rather than wording, practical advice, and a report of the unseen future eighth year.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p285/r1.anchor: والثالث: الإعلام بالغيب في أمر العام الثامن، قاله قتادة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p285/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p285/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p285/r4.claim: The apparent meaning of تزرعون is a prediction that they will farm continuously for seven years, aided by irrigation.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p285/r4.anchor: والظاهر أن قوله: تزرعون سبع سنين دأبا خبر، أخبر أنهم تتوالى لهم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p285/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p285/r5.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p285/r5.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī reads تزرعون as an imperative phrased as a report to intensify the obligation to carry it out.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p285/r5.anchor: وقال الزمخشري: تزرعون خبر في معنى الأمر كقوله: تؤمنون بالله ورسوله

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p285/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p285/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p285/r6.claim: The instruction to store the harvest in its husk does not make the earlier verb an imperative; it is a forecast of seven successive crops followed by advice.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p285/r6.anchor: ولا يدل الأمر بتركه في سنبله على أن تزرعون في معنى ازرعوا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p285/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p285/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p285/r7.claim: Dāʾban means continuous diligence or one's usual practice in farming.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p285/r7.anchor: ومعنى دأبا: ملازمة، كعادتكم في المزارعة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p285/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p285/r8.speaker: حفص
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p285/r8.claim: Ḥafṣ reads dāʾban with a fatḥa on hamza; the majority leave the hamza still, and both forms are verbal nouns.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p285/r8.anchor: وقرأ حفص: دأبا بفتح الهمزة، والجمهور بإسكانها، وهما مصدران لدأب

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p285/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p285/r9.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p285/r9.claim: Abū Ḥayyān derives the accusative from an omitted verb of the same root; al-Mubarrad instead connects it to تزرعون with the sense of working diligently, and another view treats it as a circumstantial phrase.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p285/r9.anchor: وانتصابه بفعل محذوف من لفظه أي: تدابون دأبا، فهو منصوب على المصدر

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p285/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p285/r10.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p285/r10.claim: ما in فما حصدتم can be conditional or relative.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p285/r10.anchor: وما في قوله: فما حصدتم شرطية أو موصولة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p285/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p285/r11.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p285/r11.claim: Storing grain in its husk preserves Egypt's wheat, which otherwise will not last two years; they should eat only what is necessary and consume the oldest stores first.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p285/r11.anchor: فذروه في سنبله إشارة برأي نافع بحسب طعام مصر وحنطتها التي لا تبقى

FARRA:v2p46/r5.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v2p46/r5.speaker: author
FARRA:v2p46/r5.claim: Some reciters read سبع سنين دأبا; the word may be intensified, as may words whose second consonant is one of the listed gutturals or hamza.
FARRA:v2p46/r5.anchor: وقرأ بعض قرائنا (سبع سنين دأبا) : فعلا

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p218#3/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p218#3/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p218#3/r1.claim: Daʾban means diligently and continuously; the hamza may be read with fatḥa, with no change in meaning, and both verbal forms are used.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p218#3/r1.anchor: {تزرعون سبع سنين دأبا} أي: جدا في الزراعة ومتابعة. وتقرأ (دأبا) : بفتح الهمزة. وهما واحد.

ALUSI-FULL:v12p254#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p254#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v12p254#2/r1.claim: حفص reads دأبا with fatḥa and most with sukūn; a light alif form is also transmitted. It is a verbal noun of toil, extended to habitual persistence, and can be a circumstantial description of the cultivators or an absolute object of an omitted verb.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p254#2/r1.anchor: قرأ حفص بفتح الهمزة والجمهور بإسكانها وقريء دابا بألف من غير همز

ALUSI-FULL:v12p254#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p254#2/r2.speaker: المبرد
ALUSI-FULL:v12p254#2/r2.claim: Al-Mubarrad parses دأبا as an absolute object of تزرعون, like قعد القرفصاء; Al-Alusi rejects that analysis.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p254#2/r2.anchor: وعند المبرد مفعول مطلق لتزرعون وذلك عنده نظير قعد القرفصاء وليس بشيء

ALUSI-FULL:v12p254#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p254#2/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v12p254#2/r3.claim: Joseph interprets the seven fat cows and green ears as seven fertile years and the lean cows and dry ears as seven famine years, during which they should cultivate diligently.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p254#2/r3.anchor: وقد أول عليه السلام البقرات السمان والسنبلات الخضر بسنين مخاصيب

ALUSI-FULL:v12p254#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p254#2/r4.speaker: بعضهم
ALUSI-FULL:v12p254#2/r4.claim: Some read تزرعون as an imperative to cultivate, cast as a report to make fulfillment sound already accomplished; the harvest instruction would then also be imperative.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p254#2/r4.anchor: المراد الأمر بالزراعة كذلك فالجملة خبر لفظا أمر معنى

ALUSI-FULL:v12p254#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p254#2/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v12p254#2/r5.claim: The command to leave grain in its ears prevents weevils from consuming it; Egyptian grain stores can be ruined after roughly two years, and the green ears may suggest this storage counsel is another imperative.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p254#2/r5.anchor: فذروه في سنبله ولا تذروه كيلا يأكله السوس كما هو شأن غلال مصر

ALUSI-FULL:v12p254#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p254#2/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v12p254#2/r6.claim: Grammarians object that an imperative harvest instruction cannot coordinate with a declarative forecast; replies treat it as independent advice, an answer to an implied condition, or understand the imperative as a report because it is Joseph's guidance.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p254#2/r6.anchor: لأنه لو لم يؤول ذلك بالأمر لزم عطف الإنشاء على الخبر

ALUSI-FULL:v12p254#2/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p254#2/r7.speaker: الكشف
ALUSI-FULL:v12p254#2/r7.claim: Al-Kashf finds the strongest reading predictive: the cultivation forecast interprets the dream, while the storage instruction interrupts it as urgent advice, making what will happen seem already present.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p254#2/r7.anchor: على أصله لأنه تأويل المنام بدليل قوله الآتي

ALUSI-FULL:v12p254#2/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p254#2/r8.speaker: بعضهم
ALUSI-FULL:v12p254#2/r8.claim: If تزرعون is instead an imperative, some treat the storage instruction as part of the dream's interpretation because the lean cows and dry ears predict eating what the fertile years produced; others regard it as advice outside the interpretation.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p254#2/r8.anchor: أن ما حصدتم الخ على تقدير كون

ALUSI-FULL:v12p255/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p255/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v12p255/r1.claim: They should leave all but the small amount needed to eat during the fertile years; the advice encourages moderation in food.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p255/r1.anchor: أي اتركوا ذلك في السنبل إلا ما لا غنى عنه من القليل الذي تأكلونه

ALUSI-FULL:v12p255/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p255/r2.speaker: السلمي
ALUSI-FULL:v12p255/r2.claim: Al-Sulami reads مما يأكلون with yā, meaning what people eat, rather than addressing the audience as 'you'.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p255/r2.anchor: وقرأ السلمي مما يأكلون بالياء على الغيبة أي يأكل الناس

ALUSI-FULL:v12p255/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p255/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v12p255/r3.claim: The seed grain is not separately excepted because the command to cultivate seven years already makes retaining seed understood.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p255/r3.anchor: والاقتصار على استثناء المأكول دون البذر لكون ذلك معلوما

BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p247/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p247/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p247/r1.claim: “You will cultivate seven years” is grammatically a report but functions as a command to farm as usual.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p247/r1.anchor: هذا خبر بمعنى الأمر، يعني: ازرعوا سبع سنين على عادتكم في الزراعة.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p247/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p247/r2.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p247/r2.claim: Da’ban means habit or, alternatively, diligent effort; Hafs reads it with fatḥa, one of two valid forms, from a verb meaning to exert oneself.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p247/r2.anchor: والدأب: العادة. وقيل: بجد واجتهاد. وقرأ عاصم برواية حفص:

BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p247/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p247/r3.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p247/r3.claim: They should leave harvested grain in its ear because it keeps longer and does not spoil.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p247/r3.anchor: أمرهم بترك الحنطة في السنبلة لتكون أبقى على الزمان ولا تفسد،

BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p247/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p247/r4.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p247/r4.claim: They should save most of the harvest and thresh only a little to eat, limiting themselves to what they need.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p247/r4.anchor: إلا قليلا مما تأكلون} أي: مما تدرسون قليلا للأكل، أمرهم بحفظ الأكثر والأكل بقدر الحاجة.

BAYDAWI-FULL:12:47/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:12:47/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:12:47/r1.claim: The seven years of cultivation proceed in the customary, continuous way; da'ban may be an adverb of state or an accusative verbal noun whose verb is understood.
BAYDAWI-FULL:12:47/r1.anchor: { قال تزرعون سبع سنين دأبا } أي على عادتكم المستمرة وانتصابه على الحال

BAYDAWI-FULL:12:47/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:12:47/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:12:47/r2.claim: Hafs reads da'ban with fatḥa, and both vowel forms are verbal nouns of persistent work.
BAYDAWI-FULL:12:47/r2.anchor: وقرأ حفص { دأبا } بفتح الهمزة وكلاهما مصدر دأب في العمل.

BAYDAWI-FULL:12:47/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:12:47/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:12:47/r3.claim: The command 'you will cultivate' may be an imperative cast as a report for emphasis; otherwise leaving grain in its ears is practical advice to prevent insects from eating it.
BAYDAWI-FULL:12:47/r3.anchor: وقيل { تزرعون } أمر أخرجه في صورة الخبر مبالغة لقوله: { فما حصدتم فذروه في سنبله }

BAYDAWI-FULL:12:47/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:12:47/r4.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:12:47/r4.claim: They should keep only a little to eat during those seven years.
BAYDAWI-FULL:12:47/r4.anchor: { إلا قليلا مما تأكلون } في تلك السنين.

BIQAI-FULL:v4p51/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p51/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p51/r7.claim: Joseph’s interpretation predicts or commands seven years of sustained cultivation, corresponding to the fertile cows and ears in the dreams.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p51/r7.anchor: فهو إخبار بمغيب , فهو أقعد في معنى الكلام , ويمكن أن يكون خبرا بمعنى الأمر

BIQAI-FULL:v4p51/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p51/r8.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p51/r8.claim: Dāʾban means carrying on steadily according to a customary course, here with sustained effort.

BIQAI-FULL:v4p51/r9.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p51/r9.speaker: أبو حيان
BIQAI-FULL:v4p51/r9.claim: Abū Ḥayyān says Joseph gives useful advice suited to Egyptian wheat, which will not keep for two years unless preserved in its ears.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p51/r9.anchor: بحسب طعام مصر وحنطتها التي لا تبقى عامين بوجه إلا بحيلة إبقائها في السنبل

DURR-FULL:v4p542/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v4p542/r7.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v4p542/r7.claim: Qatadah says Joseph left home at seventeen, spent seven years in the well and seven in prison, and stored food for seven years; they think he met his father then.
DURR-FULL:v4p542/r7.anchor: عن قتادة رضي الله عنه قال: ذهب يوسف عليه السلام وهو ابن سبع عشرة ولبث في الجب سبعا

DURR-FULL:v4p545/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v4p545/r6.speaker: عكرمة
DURR-FULL:v4p545/r6.claim: A Prophetic report marvels at Joseph's patience and generosity: although asked to interpret the cows, he did not rush out when summoned and wanted his innocence established.
DURR-FULL:v4p545/r6.anchor: عن عكرمة - رضي الله عنه - قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم لقد عجبت من يوسف وصبره وكرمه

DURR-FULL:v4p545/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v4p545/r7.speaker: ابن زيد
DURR-FULL:v4p545/r7.claim: Ibn Zayd says Joseph paired interpretation with prudent storage advice because grain left in its ear is preserved and not eaten.
DURR-FULL:v4p545/r7.anchor: عن ابن زيد - رضي الله عنه - قال: لم يرض يوسف عليه السلام أن أفتاهم بالتأويل

DURR-FULL:v4p545/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v4p545/r8.speaker: قتادة وابن جريج
DURR-FULL:v4p545/r8.claim: Qatadah says Joseph intended to preserve the grain; Ibn Jurayj notes an early reading that it lasts longer in its ear and is not eaten.
DURR-FULL:v4p545/r8.anchor: عن قتادة رضي الله عنه في قوله {فذروه في سنبله} قال: أراد يوسف عليه السلام البقاء

DURR-FULL:v4p545/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v4p545/r9.speaker: زيد بن أسلم
DURR-FULL:v4p545/r9.claim: Joseph used to serve a man food for two, leaving half uneaten each day; when the man ate the whole serving, Joseph recognized the first hard year had begun.
DURR-FULL:v4p545/r9.anchor: عن زيد بن أسلم - رضي الله عنه - أن يوسف عليه السلام في زمانه كان يصنع لرجل طعام اثنين

IBNABIHATIM:v7p2153/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v7p2153/r1.speaker: السدي
IBNABIHATIM:v7p2153/r1.claim: The grain should be left in its ears because that preserves it better.
IBNABIHATIM:v7p2153/r1.anchor: عن السدي : قال تزرعون سبع سنين دابا فما حصدتم فذروه في سنبله قال : هو ابقى له

IBNABIHATIM:v7p2153/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v7p2153/r2.speaker: عبد الرحمن بن زيد
IBNABIHATIM:v7p2153/r2.claim: Joseph did not stop at interpreting the dream: he advised careful management and storage in the ears, since grain in its ear is not eaten.
IBNABIHATIM:v7p2153/r2.anchor: سمعت عبد الرحمن بن زيد يقول : في قوله انا انبئكم بتاويله فارسلون . يوسف ايها الصديق افتنا

IBNABIHATIM:v7p2153/r3.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v7p2153/r3.speaker: قتادة
IBNABIHATIM:v7p2153/r3.claim: Joseph intended to preserve the harvest.
IBNABIHATIM:v7p2153/r3.anchor: عن قتادة قال لهم نبي الله يوسف

IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p286#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p286#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p286#2/r1.claim: In the dream's interpretation, cows represent agricultural years, fatness fertility, leanness drought, and ears of grain provisions.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p286#2/r1.anchor: فالبقرات لسنين الزراعة ، لأن البقرة تتخذ للإثمار . والسمن رمز للخصب

IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p286#2/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p286#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p286#2/r2.claim: Seven green ears signify seven years whose harvest is eaten fresh, with each ear standing for that year's food.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p286#2/r2.anchor: فالسنبلات الخضر رمز لطعام ينتفع به ، وكونها سبعا رمز للانتفاع به في السبع السنين

IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p286#3/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p286#3/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p286#3/r1.claim: تزرعون predicts work they ordinarily do; mentioning their customary farming prepares for the advice that follows, and دأبا qualifies it.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p286#3/r1.anchor: وقوله : { تزرعون } خبر عما يكون من عملهم ، وذلك أن الزرع عادتهم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p286#3/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p286#3/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p286#3/r2.claim: دأب means habit and persistence; it is adverbial حال describing the pronoun in يزرعون, meaning “according to your customary practice,” and links to Q 3:11.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p286#3/r2.anchor: والدأب : العادة والاستمرار عليها . وتقدم في قوله : { كدأب آل فرعون

IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p286#3/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p286#3/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p286#3/r3.claim: Yusuf's interpretation also gives the king valuable public guidance on provisioning and storage; the king's dream is divine kindness to Egypt and revelation to Yusuf through the king, perhaps as the king was ready for faith and reform.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p286#3/r3.anchor: وقد مزج تعبيره بإرشاد جليل لأحوال التموين والادخار لمصلحة الأمة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p286#3/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p286#3/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p286#3/r4.claim: Keeping surplus grain in its ear protects it from weevils that attack piled grain; people should also eat sparingly in good years to save the surplus for hardship.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p286#3/r4.anchor: ليكون أسلم له من إصابة السوس الذي يصيب الحب إذا تراكم بعضه على بعض

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p250/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p250/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p250/r1.claim: Daʾban means persistently, following the customary pattern of farming; Imruʾ al-Qays’s verse illustrates it.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p250/r1.anchor: ملازمة لعادتكم في الزراعة، ومنه قول

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p250/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p250/r2.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p250/r2.claim: The seven readers generally give daʾban a silent hamza; ʿAsim opens it, and Abu ʿAmr eases the hamza in connected recitation.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p250/r2.anchor: وأبو عمرو يسهل الهمزة عند درج القراءة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p250/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p250/r3.speaker: المبرد
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p250/r3.claim: Al-Mubarrad makes daʾban the object of تزرعون, understood to imply that they work diligently.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p250/r3.anchor: عند أبي العباس المبرد، إذ في قوله تزرعون تدأبون

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p250/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p250/r4.speaker: سيبويه
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p250/r4.claim: Sibawayh instead supplies an implicit verb from the same root to govern the verbal noun.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p250/r4.anchor: وسيبويه يرى نصب هذا كله بفعل مضمر من لفظ المصدر يدل عليه هذا الظاهر

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p250/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p250/r5.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p250/r5.claim: Storing grain in the ear is a wise response to Egyptian grain that will not keep for two years otherwise; eat the oldest store first and keep the remainder for famine.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p250/r5.anchor: فإن الحبة إذا بقيت في خبائها انحفظت والمعنى: اتركوا الزرع في السنبل

SAMIN-DURR:12:47/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:12:47/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:12:47/r1.claim: تزرعون appears to be Joseph's prediction; the author rejects reading it as a command because the people already farm by habit, while preserving grain in its ear requires instruction.
SAMIN-DURR:12:47/r1.anchor: قوله تعالى: { تزرعون }: ظاهره أن هذا إخبار من يوسف عليه السلام بذلك.

SAMIN-DURR:12:47/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:12:47/r2.speaker: الزمخشري
SAMIN-DURR:12:47/r2.claim: Al-Zamakhshari takes تزرعون as an imperative in report form to make the command emphatic, supported by فذروه في سنبله.
SAMIN-DURR:12:47/r2.anchor: وقال الزمخشري: " تزرعون " خبر في معنى الأمر كقوله: تؤمنون بالله ورسوله وتجاهدون

SAMIN-DURR:12:47/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:12:47/r3.speaker: الشيخ
SAMIN-DURR:12:47/r3.claim: Al-Shaykh says the following command does not prove تزرعون is imperative: the farming is a prediction, while فذروه gives new advice.
SAMIN-DURR:12:47/r3.anchor: قال الشيخ: " ولا يدل الأمر بتركه في سنبله على أن " تزرعون " في معنى ازرعوا

SAMIN-DURR:12:47#2/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:12:47#2/r1.speaker: حفص
SAMIN-DURR:12:47#2/r1.claim: Hafs reads دأبا with a fatḥa; the others use sukūn, two dialect forms of the verbal noun of persistent labor.
SAMIN-DURR:12:47#2/r1.anchor: قرأ حفص بفتح الهمزة، والباقون بسكونها، وهما لغتان في مصدر دأب يدأب

SAMIN-DURR:12:47#2/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:12:47#2/r2.speaker: سيبويه
SAMIN-DURR:12:47#2/r2.claim: Sibawayh makes دأبا governed by an omitted verb, تقديره تدأبون.
SAMIN-DURR:12:47#2/r2.anchor: أحدها وهو قول سيبويه: أنه منصوب بفعل مقدر تقديره تدأبون.

SAMIN-DURR:12:47#2/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:12:47#2/r3.speaker: أبو العباس
SAMIN-DURR:12:47#2/r3.claim: Abu al-Abbas attaches دأبا to تزرعون because of shared meaning; the author objects that this is not a specific manner like القرفصاء with قعدت.
SAMIN-DURR:12:47#2/r3.anchor: والثاني وهو قول أبي العباس: أنه منصوب بتزرعون لأنه من معناه

SAMIN-DURR:12:47#2/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:12:47#2/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:12:47#2/r4.claim: A third parse makes دأبا circumstantial, with analyses including an intensive absolute noun, adjective position, an omitted noun such as دائبين, or metaphorical identity.
SAMIN-DURR:12:47#2/r4.anchor: والثالث: أنه واقع موقع الحال فيكون فيه الأوجه المعروفة

SAMIN-DURR:12:47#2/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:12:47#2/r5.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:12:47#2/r5.claim: The expression دأب was also treated under آل عمران 3:11.
SAMIN-DURR:12:47#2/r5.anchor: وقد تقدم الكلام على " الدأب " في آل عمران عند قوله: كدأب آل فرعون [الآية: 11].

SAMIN-DURR:12:47#3/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:12:47#3/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:12:47#3/r1.claim: ما حصدتم can be conditional or a relative pronoun.
SAMIN-DURR:12:47#3/r1.anchor: قوله: { فما حصدتم } " ما " يجوز أن تكون شرطية أو موصولة.

SAMIN-DURR:12:47#3/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:12:47#3/r2.speaker: أبو عبد الرحمن
SAMIN-DURR:12:47#3/r2.claim: Abu Abd al-Rahman reads يأكلون in third person, meaning people; it may also be a shift in address.
SAMIN-DURR:12:47#3/r2.anchor: وقرأ أبو عبد الرحمن " يأكلون " بالغيبة، أي: الناس، ويجوز أن يكون التفاتا.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p232/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p232/r1.speaker: ابن كثير ونافع وأبو عمرو وابن عامر وحمزة والكسائي وأبو بكر عن عاصم
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p232/r1.claim: These readers pronounce dāʾban with a quiescent hamza; Abu Amr drops the hamza when reciting without a pause.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p232/r1.anchor: قرأ ابن كثير ونافع وأبو عمرو وابن عامر وحمزة والكسائي وأبو بكر عن عاصم دأبا ساكنة الهمزة

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p232/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p232/r2.speaker: حفص عن عاصم
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p232/r2.claim: Hafs reads dāʾban with a fatḥa on the hamza.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p232/r2.anchor: وروى حفص عن عاصم دأبا بفتح الهمزة

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p232/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p232/r3.speaker: أبو علي
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p232/r3.claim: Abu Ali says the quiescent form is more common, while fatḥa may be a dialect form.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p232/r3.anchor: قال أبو علي الأكثر في دأب الإسكان ولعل الفتح لغة

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p232/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p232/r4.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p232/r4.claim: Dāʾban means cultivating continuously by your usual practice; it substitutes for “working diligently.”
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p232/r4.anchor: ومعنى دأبا أي زراعة متوالية على عادتكم والمعنى تزرعون دائبين فناب دأب عن دائبين

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p232/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p232/r5.speaker: الزجاج
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p232/r5.claim: Al-Zajjaj construes it as “you work diligently,” with “you cultivate” indicating the implied verb; dāʾb means persistence or habit.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p232/r5.anchor: وقال الزجاج المعنى تدأبون دأبا ودل على تدأبون تزرعون والدأب الملازمة للشيء والعادة

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p232/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p232/r6.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p232/r6.claim: One answer to Joseph's prediction without saying “if God wills” is that it came through revelation.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p232/r6.anchor: أحدها أنه كان بوحي من الله عز وجل

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p232/r7.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p232/r7.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p232/r7.claim: A second answer is that the interpretation God taught him was certainly true, so he had no doubt.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p232/r7.anchor: والثاني أنه بنى على علم ما علمه الله من التأويل الحق فلم يشك

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p232/r8.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p232/r8.speaker: ابن الأنباري
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p232/r8.claim: Ibn al-Anbari says Joseph may have intended an unspoken exception, as his brothers did when promising to bring their brother.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p232/r8.anchor: في قولهم ( ونمير أهلنا ونحفظ أخانا )

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p232/r9.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p232/r9.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p232/r9.claim: A fourth answer is that the wording functions as a command: “Cultivate for seven years.”
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p232/r9.anchor: والرابع أنه كالآمر لهم فكأنه قال ازرعوا

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p392/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p392/r5.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p392/r5.claim: The seven fat cows and green ears signify seven consecutive fertile, rainy years; cows signify years because they plow the fields that produce crops.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p392/r5.anchor: لأنها تثير الأرض التي تستغل منها الثمرات والزروع

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p392/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p392/r6.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p392/r6.claim: Store almost all harvest in its ears because this preserves it longer, and eat only a small amount gradually to save supplies for the seven barren years.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p392/r6.anchor: في هذه السبع السنين الخصب فاخزنوه في سنبله

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p449/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p449/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p449/r1.claim: Tazraʿūna is formally a report but functions as a command, intensifying the obligation by presenting the ordered action as certain to occur.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p449/r1.anchor: خبر في معنى الأمر ، كقوله : { تؤمنون بالله ورسوله وتجاهدون }

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p449/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p449/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p449/r2.claim: Dāʾban may have a still or vowelled hamza; it is a verbal noun used adverbially or as a circumstantial description of the people working diligently.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p449/r2.anchor: بسكون الهمزة وتحريكها ، وهما مصدر : دأب في العمل

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p449/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p449/r3.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p449/r3.claim: Keeping grain in its husk protects it from pests.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p449/r3.anchor: لئلا يتسوس . و { يأكلن } من الإسناد المجازي

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p449/r7.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p449/r7.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p449/r7.claim: The fat cows and green ears represent seven fertile years; the lean cows and dry ears represent seven famine years, followed by a blessed, abundant eighth year known through revelation.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p449/r7.anchor: تأول البقرات السمان والسنبلات الخضر بسنين مخاصيب

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p449/r8.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p449/r8.speaker: قتادة
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p449/r8.claim: Qatāda says God gave Yusuf knowledge of a further year.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p449/r8.anchor: وعن قتادة : زاده الله علم سنة . فإن قلت

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p42/r16.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p42/r16.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p42/r16.claim: لعلي أرجع إلى الناس means that the messenger hopes to return to the king and his people; people may instead mean the king alone, respectfully called people.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p42/r16.anchor: أي لكي أرجع إلى الناس وهو الملك وقومه , ويحتمل أن يريد الملك وحده فعبر عنه بالناس تعظيما له

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p42/r17.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p42/r17.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p42/r17.claim: The messenger says لعلهم يعلمون from hope and concern they may fail to understand, not from doubt in Joseph; he fears a false dream or rejection of its interpretation until events confirm it.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p42/r17.anchor: ولم يكن ذلك منه شكا في علم يوسف . لأنه قد وقر في نفسه علمه وصدقه , ولكن تخوف أحد أمرين إما أن تكون الرؤيا كاذبة , وإما ألا يصدقوا تأويلها

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p42/r18.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p42/r18.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p42/r18.claim: دأبا means either continuously, year after year, or according to the customary practice of agriculture.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p42/r18.anchor: فيه وجهان : أحدهما : يعني تباعا متوالية . الثاني : يعني العادة المألوفة في الزراعة

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p42/r19.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p42/r19.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p42/r19.claim: Joseph instructs them to leave most harvested grain in its ear for storage, since stored grain is not eaten in that form; the clause is an imperative, while the first clause appears indicative.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p42/r19.anchor: وهذا القول منه أمر , والأول خبر

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p42/r20.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p42/r20.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p42/r20.claim: The first clause may also be a command, and Joseph as prophet may advise people on their interests.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p42/r20.anchor: ويجوز لكونه نبيا أن يأمر بالمصالح , ويجوز أن يكون القول الأول أيضا أمرا وإن كان الأظهر منه أنه خبر

MUQATIL:12:46-47/r3.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:12:46-47/r3.speaker: author
MUQATIL:12:46-47/r3.claim: Joseph advises Egypt to cultivate continuously for seven years and preserve most of the harvest in its ears to protect it from weevils.
MUQATIL:12:46-47/r3.anchor: { فما حصدتم } من حب، { فذروه فى سنبله } ، فإنه أبقى له لئلا يأكله السوس،

NASAFI-FULL:v2p192/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p192/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p192/r1.claim: The statement 'you will cultivate' functions as a command; following it with 'leave it in its ear' proves this. The declarative form emphasizes that the command will occur.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p192/r1.anchor: هو خبر فى معنى الامر كقوله تؤمنون بالله واليوم الآخر وتجاهدون

NASAFI-FULL:v2p192/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p192/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p192/r2.claim: Dʾaban is read with a quiescent hamza or with it vowelled by Hafs; both are verbal nouns of diligent work and circumstantial of those addressed.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p192/r2.anchor: يسكون الهمزة وحفص يحركه وهما مصدرا دأب فى العمل

NASAFI-FULL:v2p192/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p192/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p192/r3.claim: Leave the harvested grain in its ear so pests will not eat it, keeping only a little to eat during those years.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p192/r3.anchor: فى سنبله كى لا يأكله السوس ﴿ إلا قليلا مما تأكلون ﴾ فى تلك السنين

ZAJJAJ:v3p113/r2.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p113/r2.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p113/r2.claim: Tazraʿūna implies tadʾabūna, working persistently; daʾb means perseverance or habitual practice.
ZAJJAJ:v3p113/r2.anchor: أي تدأبون دأبا، ودل على تدأبون

QURTUBI-FULL:12:47/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:12:47/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:12:47/r1.claim: Joseph interprets the seven fat cows and green ears as seven fertile years, and the lean cows and dry ears as seven drought years.
QURTUBI-FULL:12:47/r1.anchor: السبع من البقرات السمان والسنبلات الخضر سبع سنين مخصبات وأما البقرات العجاف والسنبلات اليابسات فسبع سنين مجدبات

QURTUBI-FULL:12:47/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:12:47/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:12:47/r2.claim: Dāʾban means successive years; grammatically it is a verbal noun used nonliterally because sowing means persevering in the customary way.
QURTUBI-FULL:12:47/r2.anchor: تدأبون كعادتكم في الزراعة سبع سنين

QURTUBI-FULL:12:47/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:12:47/r3.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI-FULL:12:47/r3.claim: Two alternative parses take dāʾban as a circumstantial accusative, meaning persistently, or as an adjective describing the seven years as continuous.
QURTUBI-FULL:12:47/r3.anchor: وقيل: هو حال أي دائبين. وقيل: صفة لسبع سنين، أي دائبة

QURTUBI-FULL:12:47/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:12:47/r4.speaker: أبو حاتم
QURTUBI-FULL:12:47/r4.claim: Abu Hatim reports Yaʿqub's hamza-vowelled reading dāʾaban and derives it from daʾiba; al-Naḥḥās says Arab linguists recognize only daʾb.
QURTUBI-FULL:12:47/r4.anchor: وحكى أبو حاتم عن يعقوب «دأبا» بتحريك الهمزة

QURTUBI-FULL:12:47/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:12:47/r5.speaker: الفراء
QURTUBI-FULL:12:47/r5.claim: Al-Farrāʾ explains the vowel on the hamza as permissible because it is a guttural consonant; the root sense is habit, supported by a line using ka-daʾbika.
QURTUBI-FULL:12:47/r5.anchor: والقول الآخر: إنه حرك لأن فيه حرفا من حروف الحلق قاله الفراء، قال: وكذلك كل حرف فتح أوله

QURTUBI-FULL:12:47/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:12:47/r6.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:12:47/r6.claim: Leaving harvested grain in its ears protects it from pests and preserves it longer, as was practiced in Egypt.
QURTUBI-FULL:12:47/r6.anchor: قيل: لئلا يتسوس، وليكون أبقى وهكذا الأمر في ديار مصر

QURTUBI-FULL:12:47/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:12:47/r7.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:12:47/r7.claim: They should extract only what they need to eat; the explicit second clause is a command, while the first appears to report but may also command sowing.
QURTUBI-FULL:12:47/r7.anchor: استخرجوا ما تحتاجون إليه بقدر الحاجة وهذا القول منه أمر، والأول خبر

QURTUBI-FULL:12:47/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:12:47/r8.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:12:47/r8.claim: The verse grounds legal public interests: preserving religion, life, intellect, lineage, and property; securing them is benefit, losing them is harm, and averting harm is benefit.
QURTUBI-FULL:12:47/r8.anchor: هذه الآية أصل في القول بالمصالح الشرعية التي هي حفظ الأديان والنفوس والعقول والأنساب والأموال

QURTUBI-FULL:12:47/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:12:47/r9.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:12:47/r9.claim: The revealed laws guide people to worldly interests so they can know and worship God and attain afterlife happiness; this care is divine grace, not an obligation owed by God, according to Sunni authorities.
QURTUBI-FULL:12:47/r9.anchor: ولا خلاف أن مقصود الشرائع إرشاد الناس إلى مصالحهم الدنيوية ليحصل لهم التمكن من معرفة الله تعالى وعبادته

RAZI-FULL:v18p120#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v18p120#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v18p120#2/r1.claim: Joseph's declarative تزرعون functions as a command; a statement form makes the instruction emphatic, as in 2:228 and 2:233, and فذروه confirms the command sense.

RAZI-FULL:v18p120#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v18p120#2/r2.speaker: أهل اللغة
RAZI-FULL:v18p120#2/r2.claim: Dāʾban means continuing steadily in the same activity, here sustained cultivation over the seven years.
RAZI-FULL:v18p120#2/r2.anchor: قال أهل اللغة : الدأب استمرار الشيء على حالة واحدة

RAZI-FULL:v18p120#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v18p120#2/r3.speaker: أبو علي الفارسي
RAZI-FULL:v18p120#2/r3.claim: Abu Ali al-Farisi says most use a still vowel in دأب; the open vowel may be a dialect form, like variants in shamʿ and nahr.
RAZI-FULL:v18p120#2/r3.anchor: قال أبو علي الفارسي : الأكثرون في دأب الإسكان

RAZI-FULL:v18p120#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v18p120#2/r4.speaker: الزجاج
RAZI-FULL:v18p120#2/r4.claim: Al-Zajjaj parses دأبا as a cognate accusative, meaning that they farm continuously.
RAZI-FULL:v18p120#2/r4.anchor: قال الزجاج : وانتصب دأبا على معنى تدأبون دأبا

RAZI-FULL:v18p120#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v18p120#2/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v18p120#2/r5.claim: Another analysis treats دأبا as a verbal noun used adverbially, meaning they farm diligently.
RAZI-FULL:v18p120#2/r5.anchor: إنه مصدر وضع في موضع الحال

RAZI-FULL:v18p120#2/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v18p120#2/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v18p120#2/r6.claim: Keep all but the small amount eaten in its stalk so it remains sound and protected from spoilage and insects.
RAZI-FULL:v18p120#2/r6.anchor: ودعوا الباقي في سنبله حتى لا يفسد ولا يقع السوس فيه

RAZI-FULL:v18p120#2/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v18p120#2/r9.speaker: قتادة
RAZI-FULL:v18p120#2/r9.claim: The first seven years are fertile and the next seven years are drought, as indicated by the dream; the forecast of a further abundant year came through revelation, and Qatada says God granted Joseph knowledge of that year.
RAZI-FULL:v18p120#2/r9.anchor: وعن قتادة زاده الله علم سنة

ASAD-NOTES:12:intro/r2.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:12:intro/r2.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:12:intro/r2.claim: Unlike Genesis' romantic account of Joseph's fortunes, the Qur'anic story illustrates God's unfathomable direction of human affairs: people may hate what is good for them or love what is bad for them.
ASAD-NOTES:12:intro/r2.anchor: the Qur'an uses it primarily as an illustration of God's unfathomable direction of men's affairs

STUDYQURAN:12:47/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:12:47/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:12:47/r1.claim: Joseph’s interpretation covers the next fifteen years of Egypt’s agricultural cycle.
STUDYQURAN:12:47/r1.anchor: what would happen during the next fifteen years of Egypt’s agrarian cycle

STUDYQURAN:12:47/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:12:47/r2.speaker: R
STUDYQURAN:12:47/r2.claim: The first seven years would be fertile and abundant, so Egyptians should sow diligently.
STUDYQURAN:12:47/r2.anchor: During the first phase, the Egyptians would sow diligently for seven years, as this would be a time of great fertility and abundance (R)

STUDYQURAN:12:47/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:12:47/r3.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:12:47/r3.claim: Joseph advised storing most of the first phase’s harvest so people would have food during the second phase.
STUDYQURAN:12:47/r3.anchor: Joseph proposed to store up much of the harvest during the first phase so that the people would have food during the second phase.

TAB-FULL:v13p189/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v13p189/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v13p189/r1.claim: Da'ban means habit or regular practice; Imru al-Qays uses it of someone's customary conduct toward Umm al-Huwayrith and her neighbor.
TAB-FULL:v13p189/r1.anchor: قول امرئ القيس: [البحر الطويل] كدأبك من أم الحويرث قبلها … وجارتها أم الرباب بمأسل

TAB-FULL:v13p189/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v13p189/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v13p189/r2.claim: Yusuf advises seven years of customary cultivation and preserving the harvest in its ears, except a small amount for food; this is practical counsel to retain provisions.
TAB-FULL:v13p189/r2.anchor: عن قتادة، قال: " قال لهم نبي الله يوسف {تزرعون سبع سنين دأبا} [يوسف: 47]

TAB-FULL:v13p189/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v13p189/r3.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v13p189/r3.claim: Qatada says Yusuf's advice to sow for seven years was meant to build up reserves.
TAB-FULL:v13p189/r3.anchor: عن قتادة، قال: " قال لهم نبي الله يوسف {تزرعون سبع سنين دأبا} [يوسف: 47]

TABATABAI:12:46-49/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:12:46-49/r3.speaker: الراغب
TABATABAI:12:46-49/r3.claim: Al-Raghib defines daʾb as continued travel and, by extension, a lasting habitual practice; another reported sense is strenuous effort.
TABATABAI:12:46-49/r3.anchor: قال الراغب الدأب إدامة السير دأب في السير دأبا

TABATABAI:12:46-49/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:12:46-49/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:12:46-49/r4.claim: Accordingly, Joseph’s instruction is to farm continuously for seven years, either as a sustained practice or with persistent effort.
TABATABAI:12:46-49/r4.anchor: وعليه فالمعنى تزرعون سبع سنين زراعة متوالية مستمرة

TABATABAI:12:46-49/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:12:46-49/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:12:46-49/r5.claim: Tazraʿun is a report in the form of a command, emphasizing that they must comply; the following imperative to leave the harvest in its ears confirms this.
TABATABAI:12:46-49/r5.anchor: وكثيرا ما يؤتى بالأمر في صورة الخبر مبالغة في وجوب الامتثال

TABATABAI:12:46-49/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:12:46-49/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:12:46-49/r6.claim: Some explain storing grain in its ears as protection from insects and spoilage, since husked and cleaned grain deteriorates faster.
TABATABAI:12:46-49/r6.anchor: قيل وإنما أمر بوضعه وتركه في سنبله لأن السنبل لا يقع فيه سوس ولا يهلك

TABATABAI:12:49/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:12:49/r8.speaker: author
TABATABAI:12:49/r8.claim: The author says interpreters wrongly treat the dream as a forecast of seven fertile then seven barren years; Joseph instead states the required policy for surviving the anticipated famine.
TABATABAI:12:49/r8.anchor: لم يبن كلامه على أساس إخبارهم بما سيستقبلهم من السنين السبع المخصبة ثم السنين السبع المجدبة

TABATABAI:12:49#2/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:12:49#2/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:12:49#2/r1.claim: The dream depicts the practical measures the king must take for a coming famine: repeated planting, preserving grain in ears, and rationing reserves, rather than simply forecasting years.
TABATABAI:12:49#2/r1.anchor: أن الذي رآه الملك من الرؤيا إنما كان مثال ما يجب عليه من اتخاذ التدبير لإنجاء الناس من مصيبة الجدب

TABATABAI:12:49#2/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:12:49#2/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:12:49#2/r2.claim: Cows represent yearly provisions: fat cows picture plentiful harvests from sustained planting, lean cows picture shortages, and their eating the fat ones pictures famine consuming saved food.
TABATABAI:12:49#2/r2.anchor: فحكت السنين المخصبة والمجدبة أي الرزق الذي يرتزقون به فيها في صورة البقرة

TABATABAI:12:49#2/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:12:49#2/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:12:49#2/r3.claim: The green ears represent stores to be saved and the dry ears indicate preserving grain unthreshed; the dream shows the work required to protect food supplies.
TABATABAI:12:49#2/r3.anchor: وحكت ما يجب عليهم في حفظ ذخائر الرزق بالسنبلات اليابسة قبال السنبلات الخضر

TABATABAI:12:49#2/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:12:49#2/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:12:49#2/r4.claim: The exception allowing a little consumption is not dream interpretation but permission to use the amount needed for food during the seven productive years.
TABATABAI:12:49#2/r4.anchor: ولم يزد يوسف عليه السلام في تأويله على ذلك شيئا الا أمورا ثلاثة أحدها

TABATABAI:12:43-57#2/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:12:43-57#2/r2.speaker: الرضا عليه السلام
TABATABAI:12:43-57#2/r2.claim: A report says Joseph stockpiled the harvests, sold food during famine first for money, then valuables, livestock, servants, property, and land, and finally for people’s freedom; he then freed the Egyptians and restored their possessions and kingship.
TABATABAI:12:43-57#2/r2.anchor: سمعت الرضا عليه السلام يقول وأقبل يوسف على جمع الطعام في السبع السنين المخصبة فكبسه في الخزائن

TABATABAI:12:43-57#2/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:12:43-57#2/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:12:43-57#2/r3.claim: The author omits many similar reports about the famine economy because most do not directly serve the interpretation of these verses.
TABATABAI:12:43-57#2/r3.anchor: والروايات في هذا المقام كثيرة أغلبها غير مرتبطة بغرض تفسير الآيات ولذلك تركنا نقلها

TABRISI:12:43-49/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:12:43-49/r6.speaker: جعفر بن محمد
TABRISI:12:43-49/r6.claim: Jaʿfar ibn Muhammad is also reported to read ما قربتم.

TABRISI:12:43-49/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:12:43-49/r8.speaker: أبو علي
TABRISI:12:43-49/r8.claim: Abu ʿAli says دأبا is an accusative verbal noun supported by the sense of تزرعون: you work persistently at planting; its fatḥa may also be a dialectal variant.
TABRISI:12:43-49/r8.anchor: انتصب دأبا بما دل عليه تزرعون وفي علاج ودؤوب

TABRISI:12:43-49#2/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:12:43-49#2/r8.speaker: author
TABRISI:12:43-49#2/r8.claim: Daʾb means habit or effort; dhar and daʿ lack past-tense forms because taraka serves that function.
TABRISI:12:43-49#2/r8.anchor: والدأب العادة يقال: دأب يدأب دأبا

TABRISI:12:47-49/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:12:47-49/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
TABRISI:12:47-49/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas takes دأبا as consecutive years of planting, following the people's usual practice.
TABRISI:12:47-49/r2.anchor: أي فازرعوا سبع سنين متوالية عن ابن عباس أي زراعة متوالية في هذه السنين

TABRISI:12:47-49/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:12:47-49/r3.speaker: author
TABRISI:12:47-49/r3.claim: Alternatively, دأبا means planting diligently, or functions as an adverb meaning they will keep working at it.
TABRISI:12:47-49/r3.anchor: دأبا أي بجد واجتهاد في الزراعة ويجوز أن يكون حالا

TABRISI:12:47-49/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:12:47-49/r4.speaker: author
TABRISI:12:47-49/r4.claim: They should leave all but the grain they eat in its ears and not thresh it, because storage in the ear better preserves it from spoilage.
TABRISI:12:47-49/r4.anchor: اتركوه { في سنبله } لا تذروه ولا تدوسوه

TABRISI:12:47-49/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:12:47-49/r5.speaker: author
TABRISI:12:47-49/r5.claim: Another explanation says insects do not infest grain while it remains in the ear, whereas threshed grain spoils sooner.
TABRISI:12:47-49/r5.anchor: السنبل لا يقع فيه سوس ولا يهلك وإن بقي مدة من الزمان

THALABI:v5p226/r10.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p226/r10.speaker: author
THALABI:v5p226/r10.claim: Joseph interprets the fat cows and green ears as seven fertile years and the lean cows and dry ears as years of severe drought.
THALABI:v5p226/r10.anchor: فقال لهم يوسف معلما ومعبرا: أما البقرات السمان والسنبلات الخضر فسبع سنين مخصبات

THALABI:v5p226/r11.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p226/r11.speaker: author
THALABI:v5p226/r11.claim: Dāʾban means the usual practice; another interpretation is industriously, and both dāʾban and dūʾban are valid forms for exerting effort.
THALABI:v5p226/r11.anchor: قرأ بعضهم دأبا بفتح الهمزة وهما لغتان

THALABI:v5p227/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p227/r1.speaker: author
THALABI:v5p227/r1.claim: Joseph tells them to leave harvested grain in its husk so it will keep and not spoil.
THALABI:v5p227/r1.anchor: فما حصدتم فذروه في سنبله في [بذره] إلا قليلا مما تأكلون

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p135/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p135/r1.speaker: المفسرون
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p135/r1.claim: The seven fat cows signify seven prosperous years, and يوسف's “you sow” means “sow!”
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p135/r1.anchor: قال المفسرون (¬1): قال له يوسف: أما السبع البقرات السمان فإنهن سبع سنين مخصبات ذوات نعمة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p135/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p135/r2.speaker: صاحب النظم
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p135/r2.claim: تزرعون is a present-form response to the request for interpretation but functions as a command, as the explicit following command فما حصدتم فذروه shows.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p135/r2.anchor: قال صاحب النظم: قوله (تزرعون) جواب لقوله (أفتنا) جاء مجيء المضارع وتأويله أمر،

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p135/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p135/r3.speaker: صاحب النظم
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p135/r3.claim: The present form can also express prayer, as in 23:118; a prayer functions like a command, as in “say: Lord, forgive and have mercy.”
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p135/r3.anchor: وهذا كقوله {يغفر الله لكم وهو أرحم الراحمين} وهذا اللفظ مضارع وتأويله دعاء

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p135/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p135/r4.speaker: الزجاج
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p135/r4.claim: دأب means persistence in something or habitual practice.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p135/r4.anchor: قال الزجاج (¬2): الدأب الملازمة للشيء والعادة.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p135/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p135/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p135/r5.claim: Here دأبا means seven consecutive years.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p135/r5.anchor: قال ابن عباس (¬4): يريد سبع سنين متوالية.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p135/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p135/r6.speaker: أهل المعاني واللغة
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p135/r6.claim: دأب means continuing in a habitual activity; the years of sowing are successive, or it means sow according to your usual practice.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p135/r6.anchor: وقال أهل المعاني واللغة (¬5): الدأب استمرار الشيء على عادة، وهو دائب يفعل كذا،

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p135/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p135/r7.speaker: أبو علي الفارسي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p135/r7.claim: The more common pronunciation has a silent second consonant; the open vowel may be dialectal, like shamʿ/shamʿ and nahr/nahr.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p135/r7.anchor: قال أبو علي الفارسي (¬1): الأكثر في دأب الإسكان، فلعل الفتح لغة فيكون كشمع وشمع

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p135/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p135/r8.speaker: الفراء
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p135/r8.claim: Al-Farrāʾ allows a silent second consonant to take a vowel when it is a guttural consonant.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p135/r8.anchor: قال الفراء (¬2): وكل حرف فتح أوله وسكن ثانية فتثقيله جائز إذا كان أحد حروف الحلق.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p135/r9.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p135/r9.speaker: الزجاج
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p135/r9.claim: Al-Zajjāj reports Kufan grammarians allow this vowel change with gutturals, while Basrans allow only forms heard in usage, not unattested forms.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p135/r9.anchor: قال الزجاج (¬3): ذكر جميع الكوفيين أن كل ما كان ثانيه حرفا من حروف الحلق وكان مسكنا مفتوح الأول،

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p135/r10.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p135/r10.speaker: الفراء
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p135/r10.claim: Al-Farrāʾ parses دأبا as an accusative verbal noun from an implied تدأبون, indicated by the labor of sowing and by تزرعون.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p135/r10.anchor: وانتصب (دأبا) على معنى تدأبون دأبا، ودل على تدأبون تزرعون

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p135/r11.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p135/r11.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p135/r11.claim: Other grammarians parse دأبا as a verbal noun used circumstantially, meaning that they sow persistently.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p135/r11.anchor: وقال غير الكوفيين: دأبا مصدر وضع في موضع الحال، تقديره: تزرعون دائبين،

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p136/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p136/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p136/r1.claim: Thresh only what you intend to eat; leave the rest in its ears so it will not be attacked by pests.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p136/r1.anchor: قال ابن عباس (¬5): يريد كل ما # أردتم أكله فدوسوه، ودعوا الباقي في سنبله لا يتسوس.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p136/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p136/r2.speaker: المفسرون
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p136/r2.claim: Grain lasts longer and spoils less when kept in its ear, so Joseph advised the more prudent storage method.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p136/r2.anchor: وقال المفسرون (¬1): إنما قال (فذروه في سنبله)؛ لأنه أبقى له وأبعد من الفساد،

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p136/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p136/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p136/r3.claim: Exegetes disagree whether Joseph's interpretation came from knowledge God had taught him or direct revelation; the prediction of an unasked-for abundant year supports direct revelation.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p136/r3.anchor: واختلفوا في أن جواب يوسف كان من علمه أو بوحي من الله تعالى؟ فذهب بعض المفسرين إلى أنه بنى على ما علمه الله

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:12:47-50/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:12:47-50/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:12:47-50/r1.claim: Joseph's prescription is to plant continuously for seven years, corresponding to the seven fat cows, and leave most harvested grain in its ear to preserve it.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:12:47-50/r1.anchor: أي: ازرعوا { سبع سنين دأبا } متتابعة

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:12:47-50/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:12:47-50/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:12:47-50/r2.claim: They should thresh only the small amount they need to eat.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:12:47-50/r2.anchor: إلا قليلا مما تأكلون } فإنكم تدوسونه

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:12:47/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:12:47/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:12:47/r1.claim: Joseph forecasts seven years of abundance and advises sowing grain annually, setting aside food and seed, and storing the remaining harvest in its ears.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:12:47/r1.anchor: her sene bolca hububat ekmelerini, kaldıracakları ürünlerden sadece yiyeceklerini ve tohumluklarını ayırıp kalanları başak halinde depolamalarını tavsiye etti

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: Tazraʿūn is grammatically a declarative, but it functions as an imperative, a style suited to advice and guidance and paralleled elsewhere in the Qur'an.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: occurs as an enunciative (khabar) but implies the imperative.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: Joseph supplied a practical drought strategy in addition to interpreting the dream.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: not only told them the interpretation of the dream but also guided them to a practical suggestion to combat the seven years of drought.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: Leaving grain in its ears protects it from termites, insects, and other damage while it is stored.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: as long as the corn is in the ears, they remain secure from termite, insects and other calamities.

TABATABAI:12:56-57/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:12:56-57/r5.speaker: تفسير القمي
TABATABAI:12:56-57/r5.claim: Al-Qummī reports the king’s dream of seven fat cows eaten by seven lean cows and seven green ears with dry ones; the cupbearer recalled it after a time, and Joseph interpreted seven plentiful years, seven famine years, then rain.
TABATABAI:12:56-57/r5.anchor: ثم إن الملك رأى رؤيا فقال لوزرائه إني رأيت في نومي سبع بقرات سمان

TABATABAI:12:56-57/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:12:56-57/r6.speaker: أبو عبد الله عليه السلام
TABATABAI:12:56-57/r6.claim: Al-Qummī’s report has al-Ṣādiq explain that harvest should remain in its ears through seven years so it keeps, with only a little eaten.
TABATABAI:12:56-57/r6.anchor: قال يوسف تزرعون سبع سنين دأبا فما حصدتم فذروه في سنبله إلا قليلا مما تأكلون

TABATABAI:12:56/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:12:56/r2.speaker: أبو عبد الله عليه السلام
TABATABAI:12:56/r2.claim: Al-Ṣādiq’s reported wording is “what you bring near for them” rather than “what you laid up”; the commentary glosses this as approximating the harvest in revelation’s ordering.
TABATABAI:12:56/r2.anchor: وقوله عليه السلام إنما نزل ما قربتم لهن أي إن التقديم بحسب التنزيل بمعنى التقريب

IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p194#2/r4.author: Ibn Khālawayh (attr.)
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p194#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p194#2/r4.claim: Sukūn in daʾban marks a verbal noun, while fatḥa marks a noun; the opening vowel may also have been reduced for ease in a guttural environment.
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p194#2/r4.anchor: فالحجة لمن أسكن أنه أراد المصدر والحجة لمن فتح أنه أراد الاسم

IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p194#2/r5.author: Ibn Khālawayh (attr.)
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p194#2/r5.speaker: author
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p194#2/r5.claim: Daʾb means continuous perseverance, adherence, or habitual practice; al-Kumayt’s line uses it for persistent travel.
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p194#2/r5.anchor: والدأب معناه المداومة على الشيء وملازمته والعادة قال الكميت

IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p194#2/r6.author: Ibn Khālawayh (attr.)
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p194#2/r6.speaker: author
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p194#2/r6.claim: The author prefers sukūn in daʾban because the same word is consistently read that way in the phrase about Pharaoh’s people.
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p194#2/r6.anchor: والاختيار السكون لإجماعها عليه في قوله

IBNMUJAHID:v1p347/r5.author: Ibn Mujāhid
IBNMUJAHID:v1p347/r5.speaker: author
IBNMUJAHID:v1p347/r5.claim: The listed readers quiesce the hamza in dʾaban; Abū ʿAmr drops hamza when reading in connected flow.
IBNMUJAHID:v1p347/r5.anchor: 14 واختلفوا فى إسكان الهمزة وتحريكها وإسقاطها من قوله ﴿ دأبا ﴾ 47
